c3.amd_example.intro: Student asked AI to extract common themes from three papers. AI presented three themes:

items.text: Theme 1: "Sleep disruption as a mediator between screen time and adolescent anxiety"
items.reason: Matches the original papers. Usable as starting point for first outline section.

items.text: Theme 2: "The role of parental monitoring in mitigating digital harm"
items.reason: Direction is correct but AI generalized "social media exposure" into "digital harm." Corrected to "social media exposure." Original paper re-checked.

items.text: Theme 3: "Broader implications for public health policy"
items.reason: I asked for common themes, not implications. This topic does not appear in the papers. AI fabricated it. Deleted. Record: "AI exceeded request scope by adding implications."

c3.amd_example.title: Worked example — Common theme extraction

lines: You are an academic literature analysis assistant
for a first-year psychology student.
Identify the common themes across the following
three journal articles. Focus on overlapping
research topics, not methodological similarities.
I am writing a literature review for my psychology
course. I have read all three papers.
I am currently at the stage of organizing my sources
before drafting an outline.
Do not summarize each paper individually.
Do not suggest an outline or structure.
Stay at the level of theme identification only.
1. Read the three abstracts I provide below.
2. Identify recurring topics or constructs.
3. Group them into distinct themes.
Example theme format:
"Sleep disruption as a mediator between screen time
and adolescent anxiety (Paper A, Paper C)"
A numbered list of 3–5 common themes.
Each theme in one sentence, with the relevant
paper(s) noted in parentheses.

slots.c3.critique.read: Student asked "Extract the common themes from these three papers." AI returned three paragraphs. Observation: AI identified three themes, assigned papers to each, and wrote in paragraph form.
slots.c3.critique.decide: Themes 1 and 2 are usable as starting points. Theme 3 is discarded. The implications section is deleted. Theme 2's paper assignment needs verification — may re-prompt after checking the original.
slots.c3.critique.verify: Checking Paper A: AI's first theme is correct but was a secondary point, not the core finding. The third theme uses phrasing that doesn't appear in any original paper — AI generalized. The "implications" section covers a stage I haven't reached yet.

c3.techniques.role.bad: "Check my search string for scientific articles"
c3.techniques.role.good: "You are a search strategy advisor for academic databases. Review the Boolean search string I wrote. If there are logical errors, don't fix them directly — ask me questions about what went wrong."

slots.c3.critique.question: Are these three themes actually from the papers, or did AI generalize? Is the third theme too broad? Paper B is assigned to two themes — is that accurate? I only asked for common themes, but AI added "implications" — did it exceed my request scope?
slots.c3.full_example_title: Full worked example — Common theme extraction from three papers

c3.techniques.few_shot.good:
"Summarize each paper's core claim in one sentence, like this:
Smith (2022): Social media use is positively associated with anxiety in adolescents, mediated by sleep disruption.
Do the same for the remaining three papers."

c3.techniques.output_format.good: "Create a comparison table for these three papers. Columns: author/year, research question, methodology, key findings, limitations. One sentence per cell."

c3.techniques.chain_of_thought.bad: "Are the conclusions of these two papers contradictory?"
c3.techniques.chain_of_thought.good: "Determine whether the conclusions of these two papers contradict each other. First, summarize each paper's core claim. Then compare where they overlap and where they differ. Finally, explain step by step whether the difference is a genuine contradiction or a difference in scope or conditions."

c3.techniques.clear_instruction.good: "Summarize this paper's main argument and research methodology in two sentences each. This is for an undergraduate psychology class presentation."

c3.techniques.task_decomposition.good: Step 1: "Extract the common themes from the five papers I read" → Step 2: "Map the relationships between those themes" → Step 3: "Suggest possible outline structures based on those relationships"
